projects.name: Deliver capacity-building programs, technical assistance, and knowledge tools to enable government institutions and civil society organizations to effectively engage with international and regional human rights mechanisms.
projects.description: During 2026, OHCHR in partnership with national institutions, civil society organisations and the media, strengthened the capacity of government institutions and civil society to engage effectively with international and regional human rights mechanisms, including the Universal Periodic Review (UPR). National Commission for Human Rights commissioners and staff, parliamentary human rights committee members and staff, civil society organisations and journalists benefited from targeted capacity-building, technical assistance and dialogue as core strategies to improve reporting, monitoring and oversight of human rights commitments. Specifically, training for the National Commission and the parliamentary committee strengthened reporting, monitoring and oversight skills and produced draft UPR action plans and evaluation reports. Journalists were trained, with PAX PRESS, on human rights reporting and UPR dissemination. With NUDOR, 30 participants from government, UN agencies, civil society, grassroots groups and development partners discussed implementation of UPR recommendations on the rights of persons with disabilities. A workshop with Coalition Umwana ku Isonga and UNICEF brought together government institutions, civil society, the National Commission and UN agencies on implementing child rights-related UPR recommendations. In September, a high-level meeting with GLIHD on civil society engagement with human rights mechanisms produced practical recommendations to strengthen government–civil society dialogue and coordinated monitoring and reporting. These interventions improved the knowledge and skills of national actors, strengthened coordination between government and civil society, and supported national ownership of follow-up to UPR recommendations.

UN WOMEN: Addressing the underrepresentation of women in leadership particularly at the local level, in executive roles, and across key sectors is crucial for fostering inclusive decision-making and strengthening accountability for gender equality. Promoting women’s leadership is also essential for achieving equality in governance, driving sustainable development, and ensuring that policies and decisions reflect the needs of all members of society. To this end, UN Women will strengthen the capacity of National Gender Machinery institutions,  strenthen gender accountability platforms, and policy dialogues. The progress achieved under the Gender Seal program, along with efforts to meaningfully engage men and boys in advancing gender equality, will be scaled up and sustained.

Additionally, to further enhance women’s leadership, UN Women will invest in capacity building, mentorship, and advocacy. projects.description: Technical assistance provided to; and collaborated with NAEB, RICA and other agencies / National Trade Facilitation Committee in Simplifying trade and reducing export costs. The USD 100 coffee export licence fee was abolished, and export licence validity extended from one to five years for coffee, tea and horticultural products. Documentary requirements were reduced, grouped licences introduced for horticultural products, and risk-based inspections introduced by NAEB to focus checks on high-risk consignments. ITC’s technical assistance related to the Rwanda Trade Information Portal expanded access to trade procedures, recording 64,788 active users, with 23 procedures documented. Continued engagement through the National Trade Facilitation Committee advanced priorities for leather-export simplification, electronic certification, joint inspections and integration of NAEB and RICA systems.

projects.description:
1- Under this output, the ILO, Rwanda TVET Board, and the National Cyber Security Authority are jointly developing a competency-based cybersecurity curriculum aligned with national accreditation standards. The curriculum targets Level 3 qualifications, with selected modules at Levels 4 and 5, and aims to strengthen the supply Rwandan cyber security experts at the high school level. 
The activity includes a 20-day Training of Teachers (ToT) to build their instructional capacity. The programme will be piloted in two TVET schools, reaching 60 students. 
A dedicated delivery team, comprising ILO experts, national consultants, and staff from RTB and NCSA, is currently overseeing the curriculum design and accreditation process. The pilot is expected to conclude in March 2026, after which findings will inform national scale-up.

2- Through the Innovate4DigiJobs initiative, the ILO and the ICT Chamber partnered with five implementing institutions to sustainably expand access to digital skills development to collectively reach over 300 direct beneficiaries through structured training, mentorship, and job linkages.
Each partner is implementing a tailored programme that leads to an integrated approach to respond to specific local needs at the district level and different target groups. The Code and Design Alliance is providing intensive training and mentorship enabling 60 young Rwandans to access digital freelancing and online employment opportunities. The Rwanda Organization of Persons with Physical Disabilities and Wheelchair Users is delivering the Digital Empowerment for Youth with Physical Disabilities (DEYPD) programme, equipping 60 young persons with disabilities with digital literacy and employability skills. The College Baptiste Gacuba II TVET School is establishing a Digital Agri-Innovation and Youth Empowerment Hub to train 60 youth in using digital tools to improve agricultural productivity and rural enterprise creation. The Rwanda Polytechnic – Kigali College is implementing the Smart Skills Hub for Youth Employment in Digital-Economy Transformation, linking 60 TVET graduates to demand-driven training and job placement opportunities. Finally, Igire Rwanda is delivering the She Can Code programme, advancing 60 women’s participation in coding and technology careers.

Through these partnerships, the ILO ensures a balanced coverage across priority districts, combining technical training, employability coaching, and exposure to digital work opportunities. The initiatives reinforce national efforts to promote digital inclusion and contribute to the project’s broader objective of creating decent jobs for young people in Rwanda’s digital economy.

projects.name: Youth entrepreneurs trained on advanced business management and digitalization, financial literacy and productivity
projects.description:
Under this sub-output, significant progress was achieved in expanding access to quality Business Development Services (BDS). 

The ILO's Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB) and Digitalise Your Business (DYB) training materials were fully adapted to the Rwandan context and translated into Kinyarwanda to ensure inclusivity and accessibility at the district level. 

All nine manuals (in English and Kinyarwanda) were digitized to be integrated into national e-learning platforms, contributing to the long-term sustainability of training delivery. The first integration was as part of the Rwanda Polytechnic Innovation Hub e-learning platform. These efforts are ongoing to reach more e-learning platforms across the country.

A total of 44 trainers from government and social partner institutions completed the Training of Trainers (ToT) , with 50 per cent now certified to deliver SIYB and DYB independently. The remainder expected to finalize their certification in early 2026. 

To strengthen outreach, the ILO established partnerships with three BDS providers—Hanga Hubs, Kina Rwanda, and Imanzi Business Institute—who have roll out the SIYB/DYB training at the district level. Through these partnerships, over 450 youth-owned businesses have already benefited from enhanced capacities in business planning, financial management, marketing, and digitalization.

The output remains on schedule, with further expansion of partnerships and roll-out of digital learning modules planned for 2026, targeting an additional 550 youth entrepreneurs.

OHCHR is now supporting implementation, which strengthens institutional coordination and the mainstreaming of human rights into development planning. A UNCT roadmap and implementation matrix is under validation, and validation of the government-led national implementation roadmap is scheduled for November 2026. OHCHR also supported the drafting of the National Human Rights Action Plan, led by the Ministry of Justice, including its Business and Human Rights chapter finalised in December 2025. These are key milestones in advancing national integration and rights-based peacebuilding.
